# SB-1034 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses an increased hazard of airborne dust generated during blasting operations adjacent to and upstream of the heat treat hydraulic forging press EQ-P1-L4-HP02. The blasted media has been observed to migrate onto press surfaces and into enclosure plenums, creating a respirable dust exposure risk to operators and maintenance personnel and a contamination risk to hydraulic and mechanical systems. Airborne particulate can impair visibility, increase slip and trip risk on walkways and platforms, abrade seals and fittings, and accelerate wear in pneumatic and hydraulic components. In addition to occupational exposure concerns, dust ingress into the press control cabinet and into hydraulic elements may lead to unexpected mechanical behavior and increased maintenance actions.

Background and rationale
Recent shop-floor observations and a targeted inspection found dust accumulation in service areas near EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Blasting media size and composition contribute to suspension in the work environment and to secondary dust generation when media-laden surfaces are disturbed. The combination of blasting activity, personnel traffic, and press operation creates multiple vectors for dust transfer. Controls are required to reduce inhalation risk, prevent equipment contamination, and maintain the reliability of safety-critical fasteners and hydraulic components.

This bulletin aligns with the mechanical maintenance guidance in MM-P1-L4-HP02 and MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and references the engineering change ECN-2026-047 for enclosure modifications intended to reduce particulate ingress. The following controls are focused on preventing dust generation at source, containing migration, protecting personnel, and preserving equipment integrity.

Affected equipment
Primary affected equipment:
- Heat treat hydraulic forging press identified as EQ-P1-L4-HP02.

Secondary affected areas:
- Local blast area upstream of EQ-P1-L4-HP02.
- Adjacent walkways, platforms, and service access points used for press operation and maintenance.
- Hydraulic and control enclosures associated with EQ-P1-L4-HP02.

Required controls
Containment and source control
- Implement a blasting containment protocol that prevents migration of media toward EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Use local containment curtains or temporary enclosures during blasting operations to limit drift of particulate into adjacent work cells. Consult ECN-2026-047 for approved enclosure modifications and installation guidance.
- Where possible, schedule blasting activities to minimize concurrent operations that require access to EQ-P1-L4-HP02 service points.

Housekeeping and surface cleaning
- Increase frequency of dry vacuum cleaning in the vicinity of EQ-P1-L4-HP02 using vacuum equipment rated for fine particulate control. Do not use compressed air for cleaning press surfaces, components, or enclosures due to the risk of aerosolizing settled dust.
- Wipe down exposed hydraulic fittings, connector faces, and accessible mechanical surfaces prior to maintenance actions to remove accumulated dust.

Personal protection and work practices
- Require appropriate respiratory protection for personnel performing blasting, cleanup, or maintenance operations near EQ-P1-L4-HP02 where engineering controls cannot fully eliminate airborne particulate. Select respiratory protection per the site respiratory protection program and associated medical clearance requirements.
- Use designated, cleaned tools and gloves when entering press penetrations or removing access panels to prevent cross-contamination from blast media on clothing or tool surfaces.

Equipment protection and maintenance
- Before any maintenance activity that opens hydraulic systems or exposes internal seal faces on EQ-P1-L4-HP02, clean the immediate work area and the external surfaces of access points to mitigate ingress of particulate during disturbance.
- Confirm that enclosure seals and filter elements meet the upgraded specifications referenced in ECN-2026-047 and the maintenance procedures in MM-P1-L4-HP02 and MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2. Replace any degraded seals or filter elements prior to resuming blasting activities in adjacent areas.
- When reassembling components after maintenance, apply the main ram bolt torque for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 as specified: the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m. Record torque values in maintenance records per MM-P1-L4-HP02.

Monitoring and verification
- Conduct post-blast inspections of the EQ-P1-L4-HP02 exterior, enclosures, and service access points to verify that containment measures were effective and to identify any ingress points needing remediation.
- Perform functional checks of hydraulic and electronic systems after cleaning and prior to full production restart.

Examples and scenarios
- Example scenario: Blasting conducted without containment led to visible dust accumulation on press guard panels and near hydraulic hose runs. Following this bulletin, a temporary curtain was installed between the blast booth and the press area; vacuuming and panel cleaning were completed prior to maintenance, and no particulate ingress into hydraulic connections was observed.
- Example scenario: During maintenance, an access panel was removed without prior cleaning and particulate fell into a hydraulic port. The port was cleaned, but a delay in reassembly occurred while contamination mitigation steps were implemented. This bulletin emphasizes precleaning and use of cleaned tools to prevent this situation.

Records to keep
- Maintain a record of pre-maintenance cleaning actions, including the areas cleaned and the equipment used. Reference these entries in the maintenance log per MM-P1-L4-HP02.
- Record the torque application for the main ram bolt on EQ-P1-L4-HP02 using the exact value specified above and store the entry in the equipment maintenance file per MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.
- Keep inspection reports following blasting events that describe containment performance and any corrective actions taken. Retain copies with the EQ-P1-L4-HP02 maintenance records.

Responsibilities
- Maintenance supervisors will ensure torque application and records are completed in accordance with MM-P1-L4-HP02 and MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.
- Process engineers and the blasting lead will implement containment measures per ECN-2026-047 and verify compliance before blasting begins.
- Safety personnel will verify respiratory protection and provide guidance on cleaning methods that minimize aerosolization.

Effective date
Effective immediately. Implement the required controls for all blasting and maintenance activities that could affect EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and apply the maintenance and recordkeeping practices cited in MM-P1-L4-HP02, MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2, and ECN-2026-047.
